manual.coke_oven.line2: {0}The Coke Oven is the first important machine on the engineer's journey.{1}
manual.coke_oven.line3: The brick oven heats up fuels in a low-oxygen environment, pyrolyzing them into a more carbon-rich version, such as §2Coal Coke§r, or §2Charcoal§r.{0}
manual.coke_oven.line4: A byproduct of this process is {0}Creosote Oil{1}, which is used as a {2}preservative for wood{3}. This preserved wood serves as a basic construction material all throughout.{4}
manual.coke_oven.line5: The coking process is §oslow§r, but works in batches, allowing up to §216 pieces of coal§r or §28 wooden logs§r to be processed at the same time.
manual.coke_oven.line6: As such, it's recommended to build multiple ovens and stock them with enough fuel to be efficient.{0}
manual.coke_oven.line7: The Coke Oven can be automated to facilitate a more industrial scale of fuel and oil production.{0}
manual.coke_oven.line8: Items can be inserted and extracted by use of hoppers or {0}conveyor belts{1}.{2}
manual.coke_oven.line9: The creosote oil can be extracted by use of a {0}fluid pump{1}, as the oven will §onot§r output it automatically.{2}
manual.coke_oven.line10: {0}To form a Coke Oven, arrange 27 of these blocks in a 3x3x3 cube, and right-click one of the sides' center blocks with an Engineer's Hammer.
